newsitem.title: POLAND: IB AUSTRIA SEES WEDEL '97 NET UP 35 PCT.
newsitem.headline: IB AUSTRIA SEES WEDEL '97 NET UP 35 PCT.

text.p: Polish confectioner Wedel SA, 83-percent controlled by PepsiCo , should lift 1997 net profit 34.6 percent to 51.7 million zlotys, IB Austria Securities in Warsaw said in a report.

IB Austria said Wedel's 1998 net profit should rise 36.1 percent to 70.3 million zlotys while sales would rise to 871.4 million zlotys in 1997 and 1.2 billion zlotys in 1998 from 649.9 million zlotys in 1996.

"The driving force of sales growth will continue to be salty snacks, whose production we see as the main factor of the growth of the value of the firm in the next few years," the report dated July 4 and released to the press on Monday said.
Wedel netted 17.2 million zlotys in this year's first half against 8.2 million in the same period in 1996.
IB Austria said Wedel's price-earnings ratio would rise to 22.1 this year and fall to 16.3 next year from 18.3 last year.

It said the firm's decision to transform itself into a holding group encompassing four main subsidiaries would allow it to defend its position in various market segments and more quickly respond to changes in a given market.
Last week the firm's shareholders accepted management's proposal to create four fully-owned subsidiaries specialising in producing chocolate, salty snacks, biscuits and sweets.
